_what: Synthetic examples the REA hub is seeded with (tool:keep-a-reverse-engineered-thing, action seed). Every thing, handle and address here is made up; the .example addresses are reserved and reach nothing. Each row is checked against rea-hub.json by the same rules as a submission.

rows.thing: Onboarding of a made-up note-taking app
rows.notes: Seen: three screens before sign-up, each asking one question (what you write, how often, where you keep it now); the answers pick the first template shown. Inferred: the questions exist to fill the first page, not to segment, because the answers are never shown again.

rows.thing: Pricing page of a fictional analytics service
rows.notes: Seen: three plans priced by tracked events, the middle plan marked most popular, yearly billing pre-selected with the saving in money rather than percent. Inferred: the free plan's event cap sits just under what a small site sends in a month.

rows.thing: Referral loop of a made-up meal-kit service
rows.notes: Seen: each delivery box carries a card with a code worth one free box for a friend and a credit for the sender; the code page shows the sender's name. Inferred: the loop is tied to the physical box, so it fires once a week per customer.

rows.thing: Public API of a fictional weather widget
rows.notes: Seen: one JSON endpoint per place, cached for ten minutes, with the forecast hours as an array. Inferred: the widget polls on page load only, as the cache header and the update times line up.

rows.thing: Launch day of a made-up Show HN post
rows.notes: Seen: the post went up at 14:00 UTC with a one-line title, a demo with no sign-up and the maker answering every comment in the first two hours. Inferred: most of the first-day sign-ups came from the demo link, as the site's own counter moved with the post's points.
